newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Blue chip firms drive Moroccan bourse lower.
newsitem.headline: Blue chip firms drive Moroccan bourse lower.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange ended the week on Friday lower, pulled down by blue chip companies, including Societe Nationale d'Investissement, brokers said.
The all-share index closed at 436.30 points, down 0.32 percent from 437.73 points a week earlier, a bourse official said.
SNI, Morocco's second largest private conglomerate, was traded at 560 dirhams compared with 570 dirhams last Friday.

"Overall the market maintains nearly the same level as the week before. The largest capitalisation companies remained stable except for SNI which lost 10 dirhams in one week," a Casablanca-based stockbroker said.
But market analysts believe the conglomerate shares will stabilise around 560 dirhams.

SNI fluctuation coincided with the announcement of 1995 (correct 1995) consolidated results. It posted $43.7 million consolidated net profits in 1995. It gave no comparative figures for the previous year.

"The management team aims at achieving a strategic consolidation of the company's portfolio on the most profitable business with careful consideration to synergy around the core activity of the holding," Mohamed Mekouar, analyst at Upline Securities said.
The market value of all SNI's holdings is around 5.38 billion dirhams indicating a value of 543.8 dirhams on a per share basis, Mekouar said.
Upline Securities forecast an average increase of 20 percent consolidated net profit to 453.6 million dirhams in 1996.
Banque Commerciale du Maroc, the market's largest capitalisation, lost four dirhams in one week to close at 694 dirhams.
Morocco largest private ONA Group remained stable at 500 dirhams during the whole week, traders said.
The group ceded its 86.25 percent in maize derivatives producer SOMADIM to British-Belgian group Amylum, a statement issued by the group said on Friday.
Established in Casablanca in 1965, Societe Marocaine des Derives Industriels du Mais (SOMADIM) registered a turnover of 96.5 million dirhams ($11.2 million) in 1995.
It posted a net profit of 8.5 million dirhams in the same period.
ONA, with holdings in more than 100 firms, showed a 20.6 percent rise in its consolidated net profit to $37.7 million in the first half 1996 compared with the first six months of last year.
Traded volume on the official market was 41.8 million dirhams compared with 23.8 million for the week to last Friday.
